predecessors.name: Kingdom of England
predecessors.text: England as conquered by William between 1066 and the fall of Ely in early 1071

predecessors.name: Duchy of Normandy
predecessors.text: continental Normandy, which Cliopatria folds into its Norman England row from 1072

successors.name: Angevin Empire
successors.text: England and the Welsh March, which Henry II took with the crown on 25 October 1154; Northumberland and Cumbria were still Scottish until 1157

ledger.x: 1072: the Norman conquest is complete and England and Normandy are one Norman dominion.
1072: Normandy passes into the Norman England row.
1085: Cliopatria adds 35 cells in mid and south-west Wales to Norman England.
1087: William the Conqueror dies; his sons divide the Anglo-Norman dominion.
1092: William Rufus builds Carlisle Castle and takes Cumberland and Westmorland from the Scots.
1094: the Normans hold the north and mid Wales cells that Cliopatria adds to Norman England (and takes from Gwynedd and Powys, which have no shape for 1094-1098).
1096: Robert Curthose pledges Normandy to William Rufus.
1097: William Rufus campaigns in the Vexin and Maine.
1099: the Maine campaign ends: in 1099 he responded to Elias de la Fleche's attempt to take Le Mans (paraphrase).
1099: the Welsh recover north and mid Wales.
September 1100: Robert Curthose returns to Normandy and the pledge ends.
1105: Henry I invades Normandy.
1106: Henry I defeats Robert Curthose at Tinchebray and holds Normandy.
1106: Henry I reunites Normandy with England.
1135: Stephen of Blois seizes the throne on Henry I's death, the Blois dynasty replacing the House of Normandy within the same realm.

1136: David I of Scotland 'invaded the north on the news of Henry's death, taking Carlisle, Newcastle, and other key strongholds', and 'an agreement was made under which David would return most of the territory he had taken, with the exception of Carlisle' (The Anarchy page; Henry I died in December 1135; the page…
1139: the Treaty of Durham grants Northumbria to David I of Scotland's son Henry.
1141: Geoffrey of Anjou takes the Norman duchy south of the Seine and east of the Risle.
January 1144: Geoffrey of Anjou enters Rouen and the contest for Normandy ends.
January 1144: Geoffrey of Anjou takes Rouen and Normandy is lost to the Angevins.
25 October 1154: Stephen dies and Henry of Anjou becomes King Henry II of England; England passes to the Angevin Empire.
25 October 1154: the Norman kingdom of England ends with Stephen's death.

wars.name: William I's invasion of Scotland
wars.outcome: William marched north against Malcolm III with a land army and fleet in 1072; at Abernethy Malcolm expelled Edgar Atheling and 'became William's man', a 'degree of subordination' of unclear extent (Cumbria and Lothian, or the whole kingdom).

wars.name: Rebellion of 1088
wars.outcome: Odo of Bayeux led the 'Rebellion of 1088' in support of Robert Curthose against William Rufus; William defeated it after Robert failed to appear in England.

wars.name: William II's invasion of Normandy
wars.outcome: In 1091 William invaded Normandy, 'crushing Robert's forces and forcing him to cede a portion of his lands'; the brothers reconciled and William agreed to help Robert recover lands lost to France, 'notably Maine'.

wars.name: Anglo-Scottish war of 1091-1097
wars.outcome: William repulsed Malcolm III in 1091 ('forcing Malcolm to pay homage'), built Carlisle Castle in 1092 and took Cumberland and Westmorland; Malcolm and his son Edward were killed at Alnwick on 13 November 1093; Edgar conquered Lothian in 1094 and in 1097…

wars.name: William II's Maine campaign
wars.outcome: William 'secured northern Maine' in 1097-1099 and 'failed to seize the French-controlled part of the Vexin'; in 1099 he answered Elias de la Fleche's attempt on Le Mans.

wars.name: Henry I's conquest of Normandy
wars.outcome: Henry invaded in 1105 and again in July 1106 and defeated Robert Curthose at Tinchebray, 'probably on 28 September' 1106; Robert was imprisoned for life and Henry became Duke of Normandy (infobox 1106-1135).

wars.name: Franco-Norman war of 1116-1120
wars.outcome: A wider conflict broke out 'probably in 1116'; Brémule was fought in the summer of 1119; 'In June 1120, Henry and Louis formally made peace on terms advantageous to the English king'.

wars.name: Welsh revolt of 1136-1137
wars.outcome: After Henry I's death 'south Wales rose in rebellion, starting in east Glamorgan and rapidly spreading across the rest of south Wales during 1137'; by the end of 1137 Stephen 'appears to have abandoned attempts to put down the rebellion'.

wars.name: Geoffrey of Anjou's conquest of Normandy
wars.outcome: Geoffrey attacked Normandy in early 1136 and in 1138, took the duchy south of the Seine and east of the Risle in 1141 and entered Rouen in January 1144.

wars.name: The Anarchy
wars.outcome: Stephen and Matilda's civil war: David I held Carlisle, Newcastle and by the Treaty of Durham Northumbria and Cumbria (returned 1157); Geoffrey took Normandy (1144); the settlement of November 1153 (Winchester or Wallingford) left Stephen the crown; he died…

certainty.note: No treaty line or survey fixes the borders of the Anglo-Norman realm on the pages opened: the Scottish border (Cumbria, Northumbria), the Welsh March and the frontier with the French royal domain are approximate throughout.
